sentences.text: Colepiocephale is a genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Alberta, Canada, meaning "knucklehead".
The genus name combines the Latin word for "knuckle" and the Greek word for "head" to describe the curled appearance of the dome.
Evidence suggests Colepiocephale was the only pachycephalosaur present in its specific time and geographic interval.
A partial skull of Colepiocephale was collected in 1923 from the Oldman Formation in Alberta by E.J. Whitaker.
The holotype specimen — the specimen the species is based on — was initially described in 1943 by Barnum Brown and Erich Maren Schlaikjer as a species of Troodon validus.
The species name lambei honors the Canadian palaeontologist Lawrence M. Lambe.
Robert M. Sullivan renamed the genus Colepiocephale in 2003 after finding it closer to Pachycephalosaurus than to Stegoceras.
Thirteen other specimens of Colepiocephale lambei have been found in the Foremost Formation, now held in various Canadian museums.
A 2009 revision identified the first specimen of Colepiocephale from the Judith River Formation of Montana.
Colepiocephale lived between approximately 78 and 80.45 million years ago, making it one of the oldest known pachycephalosaurs from North America.
Colepiocephale is considered the oldest known member of the family Pachycephalosauridae, dating to the middle Campanian stage.
In 1987, Hans-Dieter Sues and Peter Galton argued that Stegoceras lambei and S. validum were synonyms rather than distinct species.
It is debated whether other age-equivalent specimens from the Judith River Formation belong to Colepiocephale, as their identification remains uncertain.
